correctness.rationale: The finite-center formula follows by applying the factor upper profile bound separately to each central coordinate, combining the uniform-submajorization inequalities by the prior Proposition 3.1 with arbitrarily small total loss, and using Russo–Dye. For the lower bound the prior paper expressly says its partial-isometry Lemma 4.2 has an atomic type-I-infinity counterpart by the same argument. Choose the partial isometries simultaneously in finitely many factors. Their singular-value distributions add, so the rearranged direct sum commutes with the common dilation. The prior Eq. (4) gives ((N−1)/(N+1))G uniformly submajorized by the realized singular sequence; taking N to infinity yields the norm equality. The rank-one two-center example independently gives two unit singular values and norm 2^(1/q), whereas illegal global cross-center matching gives 2. The original proof's atomic counterpart is asserted, not written in full, by its cited parent; that distinction remains a proof-source limitation rather than a contrary calculation.
residual_risks: The parent paper states the atomic proof follows by the same argument but prints detailed projection construction for the atomless case. Its lemma's displayed continuous-singular-value hypothesis does not literally include compact atomic spectra; the audit relies on that explicit authorial atomic assertion, not on falsely applying the displayed atomless hypothesis.
